research_rationale:
Executive Order 12630 of March 15, 1988 (53 FR 8859, Federal Register Vol. 53 No. 53, Friday March 18, 1988; FR Doc. 88-6145) directs executive departments and agencies to evaluate the effect of their actions on constitutionally protected property rights. The held original is the machine-extracted text of the govinfo Federal Register PDF (pages 8859-8862) with title, Sections 1 to 6, the document number and the White House dateline present. Some printing runs are garbled by character recognition (for example in section 5(d) and 5(e)) but every section is present, so identity and completeness were confirmed against the text. The U.S. Code search over release point 119-121 returned the order printed as a note to 5 U.S.C. 601; that machine lead is not cited as a source because its archive bytes are not held, so the current predicate cited is the held original clause text with the bounded searches (original-plus-bounded-search route). The searches were read for coverage notes before use: the Code search found 3 mentions, the eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 found 1, and the Federal Register catalogue search found one cross-reference from Executive Order 13406 of June 23, 2006, which is a cross-reference and not an amendment or revocation. Executive Order 13406 of 2006 section 4(c) says that order is to be implemented in a manner consistent with Executive Order 12630, and Executive Order 13061 of 1997 section 1(d) directs agencies to act in accordance with it; both recite the order without changing it. No held later order amends, revokes or supersedes it. The order has no expiry or contingent end of its own. The dates in section 1(c) and section 5(c) are 1988 deadlines for first performance and are not ends.
